transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Start time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE); Marco Diaz (Redwood SE); Aisha Khan (CTO, Cobalt Works); Tom Reynolds (Staff ML Engineer); Liam O'Connor (DevOps)

Auto-generated sections (brief):
- Summary: Cobalt Works evaluating Redwood's PLG quickstart and potential move to Dedicated/Private later. Interest in free credits, onboarding speed, latency, and security posture.
- Topics: quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private, SOC2/KMS, pilot scope, benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Jenna on the Redwood side, AE. With me is Marco, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha Khan: Hi Jenna, thanks. Good, excited to learn more.
[00:09] Tom Reynolds: Hey. Quick note, we might ask some deep infra questions, Tom from ML infra.
[00:12] Marco Diaz: Great, yeah I'm happy to dig in. Quick agenda: give a 7 minute overview of PLG quickstart, talk free credits and time-to-first-token, then Marco can answer technical Qs and we'll capture next steps. Sound good?
[00:22] Aisha Khan: Yep sounds great.
[00:25] Jenna Park: Perfect. So Redwood's quickstart is basically our self-serve API path — sign up, get free credits, follow the quickstart guide, and we have sample notebooks that get you to first token in under 5 minutes for simple text gen. For prod use we recommend Dedicated or Private depending on security and latency needs.
[00:41] Liam O'Connor: Under 5 minutes? What does that involve — like do we need a VPN or anything?
[00:45] Jenna Park: No VPN for hosted. It's just API key auth. For Private (VPC) we do have a different onboarding flow and network setup. The quickstart is hosted and is ideal for experimenting.
[00:55] Tom Reynolds: What about rate limits and quotas on the free credits — is that per account or per org?
[00:59] Jenna Park: Free credits are tied to the account/org; we can set per-key rate limits. The console shows token usage and you can configure quotas.
[01:06] Marco Diaz: From a latency standpoint, hosted API typically hits ~40-120ms p50 on small models and depends on model & seq length, but for consistent low-latency at scale customers look at Dedicated. We'll share our perf deck.
[01:19] Aisha Khan: Can you clarify p50 40-120ms — that's for single token or full response?
[01:24] Marco Diaz: That's typically generation latency per request for short responses; for long streaming responses it's different. Also depends on model size, batching, and your prompt lengths.
[01:34] Tom Reynolds: Okay. Our SLO is 200ms p95 for the interactive UI. If hosted can do that for our payloads, fine, else we'll need Dedicated.
[01:42] Marco Diaz: Understood. We should try a quick benchmark. We can support a SE-led benchmark run during pilot.
[01:48] Jenna Park: Quick note on onboarding flow — you sign up, we issue free credits, then you can use curl or the SDK. We have a quickstart notebook in the docs repo. I'll send links after the call.
[01:59] Aisha Khan: What's the time-to-first-token realistically? 5 mins seems optimistic.
[02:04] Marco Diaz: 5-15 minutes is realistic for a dev to be calling the hosted API assuming the org SSO and approvals are straightforward. If you integrate SAML SSO, that adds time.
[02:14] Liam O'Connor: Speaking of SSO and security, we have strict compliance. We need SOC 2, SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. Do you support KMS/HSM?
[02:22] Jenna Park: Yes we have SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and KMS integration for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we have managed encryption in transit and at rest, and we can discuss BYOK for dedicated/private. We'll share the security pack.
[02:35] Tom Reynolds: And data retention? We need data not to be used for model training and 90 day retention.
[02:40] Jenna Park: Redwood doesn't use customer data to train models by default and you can set retention policies; we'll include that in the security docs.
[02:46] Aisha Khan: Cool. Cost is also a factor. For hosted is there a predictable pricing page we can reference?
[02:52] Jenna Park: We have usage-based pricing. For quickstart, you'll see cost in console; for Dedicated we do committed capacity with predictable monthly costs. I'll attach the pricing overview.
[03:02] Marco Diaz: On cost/latency tradeoffs — you can often tune batching and KV/prefix caching to reduce cost without losing latency. For conversational apps we recommend KV cache to avoid repeated context.
[03:12] Tom Reynolds: You mentioned KV — sometimes I see it called K-V cache or K V cash in transcripts hehe, we get it, it's the key/value cache.
[03:18] Marco Diaz: Right, sorry for the slang. Also worth calling out quantization options that can reduce GPU footprint.
[03:24] Aisha Khan: If we start with hosted and then move to Dedicated, how hard is that migration?
[03:29] Jenna Park: It's mostly config and routing at the platform level; the API remains the same. We help with model pinning and rollout. Customers typically prototype on hosted and then buy Dedicated when they need capacity/SLA.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: For Private on-prem, do you ship an appliance or an image? Network egress controls?
[03:44] Marco Diaz: We provide a customer-managed control plane and an on-prem package (container images and infra templates). Networking is configurable and we support air-gapped installs with extra steps.
[03:52] Tom Reynolds: Sounds good. For our pilot we want to measure throughput (1k qps) and p95 latency under 200ms. Can Redwood hit that on hosted?
[03:59] Marco Diaz: 1k qps on hosted is tricky because of multi-tenant batching; it's doable with Dedicated for predictable throughput. For hosted we'd run a stress test as part of the pilot to see realistic numbers.
[04:08] Aisha Khan: What's the pilot duration you recommend? 2-4 weeks?
[04:11] Jenna Park: 2-6 weeks is common. For benchmarking 2-3 weeks is fine to collect metrics.
[04:16] Liam O'Connor: Any limits on model versions or bringing your own model?
[04:20] Marco Diaz: Hosted exposes our model catalog (open models + verified ref). For Dedicated/Private you can bring quantized variants or private models subject to compatibility. We'll need to validate the model format.
[04:31] Tom Reynolds: About metrics — can we get per-route cost breakdowns and token-level traces?
[04:36] Jenna Park: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route breakdown, token cost, traces, and latency heatmaps. We'll share sample screenshots.
[04:44] Aisha Khan: Great. Any blockers for us to get started with quickstart today?
[04:48] Jenna Park: No blockers — I can send the invite link and free credits. You create an account, confirm org settings, and start with the notebook.
[04:55] Tom Reynolds: We'll probably have a couple of people try first and then escalate to a broader pilot.
[04:58] Marco Diaz: For the SE benchmark, it would help if you send a sample prompt set and expected QPS patterns — Tom, you mentioned 1k qps, any concurrency patterns?
[05:08] Tom Reynolds: Mostly lots of short interactive calls, some bursts. We'll share a tail distribution.
[05:13] Aisha Khan: Also need to confirm legal — data processing addendum and any procurement steps.
[05:18] Jenna Park: Our procurement team has standard T&Cs and DPA; I'll loop in legal.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: On networking, if we go Dedicated in our cloud, can you deploy into our VPC?
[05:26] Marco Diaz: For Dedicated we offer private peering and VPC options depending on the contract. For true Private it's customer-managed networking.
[05:33] Tom Reynolds: Anything else from our side you need now?
[05:35] Jenna Park: If you can send the sample prompts, rough QPS targets, and compliance contact, we'll get the quickstart credits out and Marco will scope the benchmark.
[05:43] Aisha Khan: We'll do that.
[05:45] Marco Diaz: One more technical note — if you have long context windows, we can recommend model/quantization profiles; that can affect memory and latency.
[05:54] Tom Reynolds: We do have some long histories for chat, about 4k tokens sometimes. Does Redwood support the longer contexts?
[05:59] Marco Diaz: Yes depending on the model. We'll advise on kernel selection and KV cache best practices.
[06:05] Jenna Park: Ok let's recap next steps.
[06:07] Jenna Park: Action items: 1) Jenna send quickstart + credits + SOC2/SAML/KMS docs; 2) Tom to send sample prompt set and QPS; 3) Marco to draft a benchmark plan and propose dates; 4) schedule a technical deep dive with the infra team.
[06:24] Aisha Khan: That works for us. Can we get pricing ranges for Dedicated?
[06:28] Jenna Park: I'll include an approximate estimate in the email; exact pricing depends on commit level and model selection.
[06:34] Tom Reynolds: Also send any playbooks for migrating from hosted to dedicated.
[06:37] Marco Diaz: We'll include a migration overview doc.
[06:40] Liam O'Connor: Okay thanks.
[06:41] Jenna Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and set up the next meeting.
[06:45] Aisha Khan: Thanks, talk soon.
